question.text: Vijay Mid-Cap Fund (Cat II): single-cash-flow deal. Capital call INR 50 crore at end-2020. Complete exit at end-2025 for INR 100 crore. What is the approximate gross DEAL-LEVEL IRR (annualised, ignoring interim fees/carry)?

explanation.text: The Logic: MOIC = 2.0x over 5 years. IRR = 2^(1/5) - 1 = 1.1487 - 1 = 14.87% p.a. This is the exact formula for single-cash-in/single-cash-out IRR. The Trap: B is simple return 100%/5yr/(100%) = mis-calc; C is the common 'double in 5 years = 20%' shortcut (actually = Rule-of-72 approximation); D is half-baked compounding. Cross-Exam Context: IRR is a universal PE/VC metric; XIX-C, XIX-A, XXI-B all test variants. Manager's Pro-Tip: Always distinguish GROSS DEAL IRR (no fees) from NET FUND IRR (post fees, carry, fund expenses). LPs evaluate NET IRR. A 20% gross deal IRR can translate to 13-15% net fund IRR after the 2-and-20 layer — budget this gap in your LP communications.
